shortTitle: No web content reaches iOS UI automation; the VoiceOver consequence is untested
userImpact: Two independent iOS automation query paths see nothing inside the WebView. On a coach dashboard visibly showing a title, a greeting, three sheet CTAs and a bottom nav, the runtime tree holds 18 elements - all full-screen unlabelled containers - and zero interaction targets, and no on-screen string resolves by text predicate. What this costs USERS is not yet established: it is proven only that this harness cannot see the app.
confidence: high that this automation harness sees zero targets. The overlay confound has been eliminated: an initial probe searched only for text sitting BEHIND an open Radix-Dialog sheet (which correctly aria-hides the background), so it was invalid; re-probing for FOREGROUND sheet text ('Not now', 'Stay in the loop', 'Enable Notifications') also resolves nothing. The VoiceOver consequence remains UNTESTED - snapshot-ui and wait-for-ui share one accessibility API family, and XCUITest, the path Xcode UI tests and Maestro drive, was not exercised and can behave differently on WKWebView.
reproductionSteps: Build Release for an iOS 26.5 simulator and launch com.helmsportslabs.golfhelm.
Let it settle (~10s). Screenshot to record exactly what is on screen, including any modal.
PATH 1: xcodebuildmcp ui-automation snapshot-ui --simulator-id <udid>. Observe 18 elements, 0 likely targets, 1 scroll area.
PATH 2: xcodebuildmcp ui-automation wait-for-ui --predicate textContains --text 'Not now' (also 'Stay in the loop', 'Enable Notifications'). All time out.

IMPORTANT: probe for text in the FOREGROUND. An earlier probe used background text behind an open sheet; Radix Dialog aria-hides the background, so that result was invalid and is recorded as such in native/waitforui-probe.txt.
Do NOT tap 'Enable Notifications' - it raises the iOS system permission dialog, which blocks automation and changes device state.
CONTROL: com.apple.Preferences. snapshot-ui returns 14 labelled targets; wait-for-ui --text General resolves.
Repeat with ApplicationAccessibilityEnabled=true. Unchanged.
NOT RUN: Xcode Accessibility Inspector, XCUITest, VoiceOver on a device.
expectedBehavior: A WKWebView is normally expected to project its web content into the iOS accessibility tree so that buttons and links appear as native elements with labels. Whether that projection is on-demand - materialised only when a real assistive client attaches - is precisely what is unresolved here.
observedBehavior: Zero web content is projected to either query path. The tree stops at the WebView's own container views. The 18-element, all-role-'other', stops-at-the-container shape is equally consistent with 'remote tree never requested' and with 'content suppressed'; nothing collected distinguishes them.
rootCauseExplanation: Not isolated. There is no accessibility-related code anywhere in the Swift shell (grep over ios/App/App/*.swift returns nothing), so this is not an explicit opt-out in Helm's code. Candidate causes, none tested: (1) WKWebView's remote accessibility tree is built lazily and may only populate once an assistive client attaches, which the AXe path may never trigger - this is the leading candidate and would make the finding a testability problem, not a user problem; (2) a Capacitor/WebView configuration suppresses it; (3) something upstream in the OS version. Determining which changes the severity by an order of magnitude.
existingContract: memory/features/ios-native-shell.md describes the native surface; accessibility is not part of any stated contract today.
historicalFindingReferences: IOS_PREMIUM_NATIVE_AUDIT_2026-08-25 P1-12 (no native XCTest/XCUITest infrastructure exists) - related but not the same claim
proposedSmallestFix: None yet - this is a bounded reproduction experiment, not a patch. Attach Xcode's Accessibility Inspector to the running simulator app and record whether it enumerates web content. If it does, the finding collapses to 'UI automation cannot select elements' (a testability problem, P2). If it does not, VoiceOver genuinely cannot drive the app and this is the most severe finding in the audit.
regressionTest: Once the cause is known: a native snapshot assertion that the bottom-nav tabs appear as labelled targets.
nativeBinaryRequired: unknown until root cause is isolated

shortTitle: 59 controls escape the design system's own 44pt tap-target floor
confidence: high. Measured in WebKit at iPhone 13 geometry across eight signed-in screens after scrolling each end to end so IntersectionObserver reveals had fired, with hidden elements and children of larger interactive ancestors excluded, and three representative cases re-verified individually against their full ancestor chain. Counts were stable across two runs (59, then 58).
userImpact: Apple's minimum comfortable tap target is 44x44pt. The good news first: the design system already honours it. Across eight signed-in coach screens, 373 of 432 visible interactive controls (86%) are at least 44pt tall, and the single most common height is exactly 44pt. The floor exists and is widely applied. But 59 controls (14%) sit below it, and they cluster in a handful of shared components rather than scattering randomly. The worst are on the roster: a per-player status toggle at 76x24 and an intent chip at 88x20, repeated once per player down the list, roughly a fingernail tall and about 2pt apart vertically. The section tab strip used on five screens is 38pt inside a 39pt nav, so there is no slack to absorb a slightly-off thumb.
sourceLocations: src/components/fairway/app-shell/ - section tab strip (38pt, appears on calendar, messages, qualifiers, roster, rounds)
src/components/fairway/ - filter chip control (30-36pt, on qualifiers and rounds)
roster player row: status toggle 76x24, set-intent chip 88x20
reproductionSteps: HELM_AUDIT_BASE_URL=https://www.helmsportslabs.com npx playwright test -c playwright/native-audit.config.ts --project=webkit-phone-signed-in
Read signed-in/*.json in the evidence directory; smallTapTargets lists every control under 44pt with its measured box.
expectedBehavior: Interactive controls on a touch screen are at least 44x44pt, per Apple HIG.
observedBehavior: 432 visible interactive controls across eight screens. 373 (86%) at or above 44pt, mode exactly 44pt (84 controls). 59 (14%) below, distributed 42pt x1, 40pt x14, 38pt x12, 36pt x7, 34pt x1, 32pt x1, 30pt x4, 28pt x1, 24pt x9, 20pt x9. The shape matters: a dense spike at 44 with a thin tail below it is a floor that exists and was missed in specific places, not an absent floor.
excludedAsNotDefects: Seven calendar day cells measure 37pt wide. A 7-column month grid on a 390pt-wide phone cannot give each column 44pt; Apple's own Calendar has the same constraint. Counted separately and NOT in the 59. Screen-reader skip links (32x16), zero-size inputs and children of larger interactive ancestors were filtered out.
rootCauseExplanation: The 44pt floor is real and dominant across the product. These 59 controls carry explicit smaller heights in their own class names -- the tab link's padding 10px/14px/12px makes 38pt, chips use min-h-[36px] and h-7 (28pt), insights CTAs use min-h-[40px] and min-h-[36px] -- so each is a local override or a component that predates the floor, not a systemic gap. CORRECTION: an earlier draft of this finding claimed no control anywhere reached 44pt. That was wrong and circular -- it was computed over the set already filtered to controls UNDER 44. Measuring all 432 controls reversed the conclusion.
existingContract: AGENTS.md Mobile UI rules: 'Reuse shared button/chip/tab/card/metric/empty-state components; no one-off spacing, radius, icon sizes, or control heights.' The components ARE shared here - the shared value is simply too small.
proposedSmallestFix: Close the gap in the shared components rather than per screen: raise the tab strip, chip, field and the two roster row controls to the 44pt floor the rest of the system already uses. Where a design genuinely needs a smaller VISUAL control, keep the visual size and extend the hit area with padding or a pseudo-element. Because the floor already exists, this is gap-closing against an established norm, not a new convention -- which also makes it far lower risk than the earlier draft implied.
regressionTest: playwright/native-audit/journeys.spec.ts already records this per screen. Turn smallTapTargets.length into an assertion once the floor is raised.
verificationLayers: physical device (a real thumb is the actual test)
backwardCompatibilityRequirement: None. Old binaries pick this up on the next web deploy.
effortClass: small-to-medium - a handful of shared components, against a floor that already exists
rollbackApproach: Revert the token and component heights.

shortTitle: The same search field is four different heights on four screens
confidence: high - measured in the same sweep, four screens, one control role.
userImpact: A search field is a search field. Here it is 40pt on messages, 32pt on rounds, 24pt on qualifiers and 20pt on roster -- and the system's own norm, the most common control height in the product, is 44pt. So all four are wrong and they are wrong by different amounts. Nobody consciously notices this, which is exactly why it reads as 'website': native apps are visually predictable, and a control that resizes as you move between tabs quietly says these screens were built by different hands at different times.
sourceLocations: roster search: input.peer.min-w-0 at 20pt inside a 36pt bordered wrapper
reproductionSteps: Run the signed-in project and grep signed-in/*.json for labels matching /[Ss]earch/.
expectedBehavior: One search control, one height, everywhere.
observedBehavior: Four heights for one control role. On roster the tappable input is a 20pt strip inside a 36pt visual box, so even the visual control is under 44 and the actual target is far under it.
rootCauseExplanation: Not traced to source this run. The measurements prove four different rendered heights; whether that is four separate components or one component with four sets of caller overrides is unresolved, and it changes the fix. Reading the four call sites answers it in minutes.
existingContract: AGENTS.md Mobile UI rules: reuse shared components, no one-off control heights.
proposedSmallestFix: Identify the four call sites, converge on the shared Fairway field component, and give it the 44pt floor from F-TAP-01.
regressionTest: Assert one height for the search field across the four screens in journeys.spec.ts.
effortClass: small once the call sites are identified

shortTitle: RETRACTED - Sign in button contrast failure was a measurement artifact
userImpact: None. This finding was wrong and is kept only so the record shows it was withdrawn rather than quietly deleted.
whatWasClaimed: That the Sign in button label sat at 3.52:1 in light and 3.61:1 in dark, below the 4.5:1 AA minimum, with measured colours #e6f2ea on #318f53 and #e8f3ec on #2f8e51.
whyItWasWrong: axe-core ran before the login form finished its entrance transition. Mid-transition the button is partially transparent, so the colours sampled were composites of the real button blended toward the cream page ground - #e6f2ea is white blended toward cream, #318f53 is #15803d blended toward cream. Neither colour appears in any frame a user ever sees. document.fonts.ready, which the spec awaited, does not wait on CSS transitions.
correctedMeasurement: With the entrance transition settled, the Sign in label is #ffffff on #15803d = 5.02:1 at 15px/600, identical in light and dark. That passes WCAG AA for normal text. Measured directly via getComputedStyle in WebKit at iPhone 13 geometry, independent of axe.
residualOpenItem: axe now reports color-contrast as INCOMPLETE for 12 nodes on this page - background gradients and image-bearing ancestors it cannot sample. Incomplete is not a pass. Those 12 are unmeasured, not cleared, and a manual check of the gradient headings remains outstanding.
correctionEvidence: webkit/results.json (entrance-settle + axe-results attachments, all three projects)
processFix: playwright/native-audit/login-audit.spec.ts now waits for the submit button's whole ancestor chain to reach opacity 1 and an identity transform before calling axe, attaches the settle outcome as evidence, and fails loudly if settling never happens.

shortTitle: autoFocus is pointer-gated in six components and ungated at most other sites
userImpact: Opening one of these sheets or modals on an iPhone throws the software keyboard up immediately, covering much of the sheet before the user has decided to type. The codebase already knows the right answer - autoFocus={finePointer} - it just is not applied consistently.
confidence: high in source; the per-surface visual consequence is not yet captured on each screen
reproductionSteps: grep -rn 'autoFocus' src/app/golf src/components/fairway src/components/golf src/components/auth
Compare against the six sites that read autoFocus={finePointer}, where finePointer = useMediaQuery('(pointer: fine)').
On the simulator, open any ungated surface and observe the keyboard rise unprompted.
expectedBehavior: A coarse-pointer device does not raise the keyboard until the user taps a field.
observedBehavior: Six components gate autoFocus on a fine pointer. The remaining autoFocus sites in the golf/fairway tree are ungated; the ones confirmed by reading each site are listed in sourceLocations. A raw grep count is not quoted here because it mixes in sites gated on unrelated conditions (autoFocus={scope === 'this'}) and a non-JSX autoFocus: true inside a date-picker options object.
rootCauseExplanation: There is no shared hook. useMediaQuery('(pointer: fine)') is re-declared inline in six separate components, so the pattern spreads only by copy-paste and every new surface starts ungated by default.
existingContract: memory/features/ios-native-shell.md documents the --keyboard-height / body.keyboard-open contract, which handles the keyboard once it is up. It says nothing about whether it should come up.
proposedSmallestFix: Extract useFinePointer() into src/hooks, point the six existing sites at it, then convert the ungated sites case by case. Some are correct as they stand - a dedicated 'add a note' page arguably should focus - so this is a per-site decision, not a sweep.
regressionTest: An ESLint rule forbidding bare autoFocus under src/app/golf and src/components/fairway, with the finePointer form as the allowed spelling.
effortClass: medium - the hook is trivial, the 22 judgement calls are the work
rollbackApproach: Per-site revert; each change is independent.

shortTitle: Player screens carry real sub-AA text contrast, confirmed by two methods
confidence: high, and deliberately double-checked because this audit already retracted one contrast finding. axe-core reported these on a settled page (the sweep scrolls end to end before measuring), and an independent in-page measurement that resolves oklab() colours through a canvas readback reproduced axe's numbers to within rounding: 4.06 vs axe's 4.05 for #d7f4db on #248342, and 4.03 vs 4.03 for #238d46 on #fff9ee. Two methods, same answer, unlike F-CONTRAST-01 where the page state itself was wrong.
userImpact: Text on the player-facing screens sits just under the WCAG AA 4.5:1 minimum - around 4.03-4.06:1 - at 12px and 15px. Six of eight player screens carry serious contrast violations, worst on my-standing with 43 nodes. The pattern is brand green on cream (#238d46 on #fff9ee) and pale green on green (#d7f4db on #248342). These are small margins, not dramatic ones, but they are real, they are on the screens players use most, and a golf app is read outdoors in bright light where the effective contrast is worse.
sourceLocations: player screens: my-standing, my-development, my-game-profile, my-insights, dashboard, calendar, messages
reproductionSteps: HELM_AUDIT_ROLE=player with the player account's credentials, then npx playwright test -c playwright/native-audit.config.ts --project=webkit-phone-signed-in
Read signed-in-player/*.json; the color-contrast entries under axe.violations are VIOLATIONS, not incomplete.
expectedBehavior: Normal-size text meets 4.5:1 against its own background.
observedBehavior: Serious color-contrast violations on 6 of 8 player screens: my-standing 43 nodes, my-development 9, my-game-profile 7, my-insights 7, dashboard 2, calendar 2, messages 1. Measured ratios cluster at 4.03-4.06:1 where 4.5:1 is required.
rootCauseExplanation: A token pair problem, not a component problem: the same green-on-cream and pale-green-on-green combinations recur across unrelated player screens. Nudging the green darker (or the pale text lighter) in src/styles/design-tokens.css clears every instance at once. The margins are small enough that a modest token change closes them.
existingContract: AGENTS.md: src/styles/design-tokens.css is the authority for --fw-* colours; tokens beat prose.
proposedSmallestFix: Adjust the offending token pairs in design-tokens.css, then re-run the player sweep. Do NOT patch individual screens - the pairs are shared, and a local fix would create a second vocabulary.
regressionTest: The player sweep already records these per screen; assert zero serious color-contrast violations once the tokens change.

confidence: high - document.title captured directly on each screen during the player sweep.

It shows in the browser tab and in anything that reads the document title. Small, but it is exactly the kind of seam that tells a user they are looking at a web page built for somebody else.

shortTitle: Sign-out silently failed on the first attempt, leaving the user signed in
confidence: the observation is certain and screenshotted; the MECHANISM is unproven and it reproduced only once in two attempts.
userImpact: Tapping Sign out showed a 'Signing out...' pending state, the sheet closed, and ~29 seconds later the app was still fully signed in on the coach dashboard with all team data visible. No error, no toast, no retry prompt. A second attempt worked immediately. The frequency is unknown; the failure MODE is what matters - a user is shown a sign-out that completes its animation and leaves them logged in. On a borrowed or shared phone that is a privacy problem, not a polish one.
reproductionSteps: Sign in as coach in the simulator build.
More tab -> Sign out.
Observe the 'Signing out...' pending pill, then the sheet closing.
Wait 30s and screenshot. Observed: still on the coach dashboard, still authenticated.
Repeat: the second attempt reached the login screen immediately.
expectedBehavior: Sign out either completes and lands on the login screen, or fails visibly with an error the user can act on.
observedBehavior: It did neither. The sheet dismissed and the session persisted, with no signal that anything had gone wrong.
rootCauseExplanation: Not isolated. Candidates, untested: the signOut call rejected and the rejection is swallowed; a race between the sheet's dismiss animation and the navigation; or a network timeout with no error path. Reproducing it under a console/network capture is the next step, not a patch.
proposedSmallestFix: None yet - reproduce first. Whatever the cause, the sheet must not dismiss on an unconfirmed sign-out, and a failed sign-out needs a visible error.
regressionTest: An e2e assertion that after sign-out the session is gone and the login form is present.

shortTitle: Deliberate mono numerals break down at display size, and are applied inconsistently
confidence: high - verified in the source token AND magnified from a device screenshot, so neither half is inferred.
userImpact: Fragment Mono's period is a square block on a full monospace advance. At display size the player's strokes-gained figure renders as '-3 [] 62' - three tokens rather than one number. The same face produces slashed zeros in the priority list (01 02 03) and the coach trajectory row (3 up, 0 flat, 4 down), and wide gapping in '-4.8 / rd'. Message previews and relative dates are mono too, which makes a chat list look like log output.
sourceLocations: src/styles/design-tokens.css:375-378 (--fw-font-mono = Fragment Mono; comment: 'Numbers stay mono')
reproductionSteps: Sign in as the player, open the Stats tab, and magnify the strokes-gained figure.
Compare with the player Rounds tab, where the same class of number (20, 74.4, 68, +2.5, 30%) is set in the sans face.
expectedBehavior: A headline number reads as one number.
observedBehavior: It reads as three tokens, and the choice is not applied consistently between Stats and Rounds.
rootCauseExplanation: Deliberate, not a leaked developer font - the token and its comment are explicit. The defect is that a small-text tabular face is being used at display sizes where its square punctuation and fixed advance stop reading as typography. The inconsistency between Stats and Rounds shows the rule was never settled.
proposedSmallestFix: Keep mono for small tabular columns if wanted, but set display-size figures in the sans face with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, which gives column alignment without the square period. Then pick one rule and apply it to both Stats and Rounds. This is a token decision, not a component rewrite.
regressionTest: None automatable cheaply; a screenshot diff on the Stats card would catch a regression.

shortTitle: The selected pill escapes its segmented control, in three places

It reads as a control that does not fit its own container - the kind of detail that makes an interface feel unfinished without the user being able to say why.

shortTitle: No swipe-back gesture, and no back button in any sub-screen header
confidence: high - eight identical frames across a full edge-drag, corroborated by the absence of allowsBackForwardNavigationGestures in ios/.
userImpact: Edge-swipe-to-go-back is the most automatic gesture on iOS and it does nothing here - no drag, no peek, no navigation. It compounds: no sub-screen has a back button either. shortTitle: No iOS translucent materials on phone, so the interface has no depth
confidence: high - the md: gating is explicit in source and the flat result is visible in both light and dark captures.
userImpact: iOS builds depth almost entirely from translucent materials: content passing under a blurred bar tells you the bar is a layer floating above a continuous surface. Here both bars are flat opaque fills on a phone. The top bar's blur is gated to md: (tablet and up), and the bottom nav's blur was deliberately removed as 'cheap chrome'. The result is bars that content simply disappears behind - which is also why F-NAVCLIP-01 reads as broken rather than as content scrolling under glass. Dark mode makes it plainest: flat grey cards on near-black with no shadow, blur or vibrancy anywhere.
reproductionSteps: Scroll any screen on a phone-width device and watch content meet the top and bottom bars.
Switch the simulator to dark appearance and look for any layering cue.
expectedBehavior: Bars use a translucent material so content is visibly blurred beneath them.
observedBehavior: Opaque fills at phone width; blur only from md: up.
rootCauseExplanation: Both are explicit source decisions, not accidents. The bottom-nav comment gives performance as the reason, which is worth re-testing on current hardware.
proposedSmallestFix: Re-enable backdrop blur at phone widths on both bars, behind a supports- query and the existing prefers-reduced-transparency guard. Measure the frame cost on a real device before accepting the original performance objection - it predates this hardware.

expectedBehavior: The scroller bounces at its limits; a dashboard offers pull-to-refresh.
observedBehavior: Locked at both edges.
rootCauseExplanation: Deliberate. globals.css's own comments explain it: overscroll in a WebView exposed the page ground behind the app and leaked cream during route changes. The lock is a real fix for a real bug - the cost is the platform's signature feel.

Four seconds to usable is slow next to a native app that restores its previous state near instantly, and cold launch is where the 'this is a website' impression is formed before the user has touched anything.
reproductionSteps: terminate the app, relaunch, and capture frames at 0.3/0.8/1.3/1.8/2.3/2.8/3.4/4.0s from one process.
expectedBehavior: No black frame; a launch image matching the first screen; usable well under 2s.
observedBehavior: Black at 0.8s; usable at 4.0s.
rootCauseExplanation: The black frame is consistent with an unset window/WebView background during the storyboard-to-web handoff. The 4s is unattributed between native start, network and hydration - it needs a trace before anyone optimises.
proposedSmallestFix: Set the window and WebView background to the app's cream so no black can show. Separately, trace the 4s to decide whether it is native start, network or hydration - do not guess.
effortClass: small for the black frame; investigation for the 4s
